"It its page of race bibliography will be especially
helpful to students and study club workers."
PAULINE SMITH,
Detroit, Mich.

"The Crisis fills a long-felt want. It should be
indispensable to every patriotic American."
R. C. EDMONDSON,
Washington, D. C.

"I have just read the last issue of THE CRISIS.
I find it valuable for the series of facts that it
presents in succinct form. I have read it with
deep interest and consider it of distinct value."
WILBUR P. THIRKIELD,
President Howard University,
Washington, D. C.

"I like THE CRISIS. This first number is good
in itself, and is full of great promise."
CHARLES T. THWING,
President Western Reserve University,
Adelbert College,
Cleveland, Ohio.

"It makes a dignified, informing and convincing
argument against color prejudice."
SAMUEL A. PEASE,
Attorney, Brooklyn.

"I feel that it supplies a long-felt necessity.
I am trying to induce all lovers of fair play for
the human race to subscribe to it."
T. M. DENT,
Dept. Commerce and Labor.

regions.text:
"I am much impressed with the appearance of your new monthly magazine."
L. J. JOHNSON,
Harvard University,
Cambridge, Mass.

"The paper is excellent and I hope I may be instrumental in securing other subscribers."
BERTHA JOHNSTON,
Brooklyn, N. Y.

"It is a splendid effort, courageous in its utterances and manly in its defense of the man of color."
GEO. E. WIBECAN, JR.
Brooklyn, N. Y.

"I read the first number of your magazine, THE CRISIS, with care and much appreciation yesterday."
W. H. SHORT,
Executive Secretary,
The Peace Society of the City of New York.

"I have read every word of the first number of THE CRISIS with a relish equal to the zeal of the production."
J. WILBUR NORRIS,
Sioux City, Ia.

"I have looked over the matter arranged for THE CRISIS and it all seems to me to be excellent. I cannot suggest any change. I shall be glad to contribute to the magazine."
CHARLES EDWARD RUSSELL,
New York.
